title: Achan's Judgment and the Capture of Ai
reflectionText: One man's plunder, buried in the ground of his tent, and a whole army could not stand before its enemies. The lot narrowed from tribe to family to household to a single name, and what was hidden was carried up into the open. What is it to belong to a people so bound together that a thing buried in secret was never only your own?
editorialNotes: Text-First Story Factory 2.0 Batch B (journey backlog G6, approved 2026-07-23). Joshua 7:13-8:29, absent both lanes. LOCKED ID/order: Achan is 1577, before the Gibeonite Covenant (1578). Opens at 7:13 (Yahweh's instruction to sanctify) so vv13-15 are not orphaned; seams from existing 1294 (Joshua 7:6-12, Joshua's grief after Ai) WITHOUT repeating its material. One coherent narrative covering both the judgment of Achan (7:13-26) and the capture of Ai (8:1-29), not two unrelated stories. SHORT+FULL+LONG (WEB 329w/518w/911w; KJV 348w/545w/929w): the 43-verse, ~1379-word two-part source honestly supports LONG (comparable-density precedent: 1572/Genesis 27). Corporate judgment stated plainly and NOT softened: Achan, his sons and daughters, his oxen, asses, sheep, tent, and all he had, stoned and burned in the valley of Achor (7:24-25). No moral commentary defending or condemning the judgment; no invented motives or emotions (Achan's coveting is his own stated confession, 7:21). Ai covered coherently: the ambush plan, the feigned flight, the burning, the twelve thousand fallen, the king hanged and buried under stones (8:29). 'Valley of Achor / valley of Trouble' rendered with the passage's own wordplay (7:25-26). Boundary held to 8:29. KJV lane uses KJV diction (accursed thing, Babylonish garment, spoil, cattle); WEB uses Yahweh.
